questions.text: How can an aeroplane's aileron be given aerodynamic balance so that the control forces become lighter?
options: By setting the hinge line back behind the leading edge of the aileron (inset hinge)
By attaching a weight ahead of the hinge line
By fitting an anti-balance tab to the trailing edge
By making the up-going aileron deflect further than the down-going aileron

questions.text: What describes the 'Dutch roll' motion of an aeroplane?
options: A coupled oscillation in which the aeroplane alternately rolls and yaws, out of phase, after a lateral or directional disturbance
A slowly tightening descending spiral that develops when lateral stability is weak and directional stability is strong
A repeating pitch oscillation about the lateral axis at constant airspeed
A one-sided roll caused by adverse aileron drag when a turn is started

questions.text: Ice has built up on the wings of an aeroplane in flight. What is the effect on the stalling speed?
options: It increases, because the ice reduces the lift the wing can produce and adds drag
It remains unchanged, because the critical angle of attack does not depend on the surface condition
It decreases, because a rough surface keeps the boundary layer attached longer
It increases only in turns, because the load factor then rises
The aeroplane's weight divided by its wing area
The wing area divided by the aeroplane's weight
The total drag divided by the wing area
The lift divided by the drag

questions.text: After an engine failure, what does a propeller that keeps windmilling in the airflow produce?
options: Drag instead of thrust, which slows the aeroplane down
Neither thrust nor drag, because the engine is no longer delivering power
Extra thrust, because the airflow keeps driving the blades
Lift that lengthens the glide

questions.text: Compared with straight and level flight, what must the pilot do to keep the same speed and altitude in a steady level turn?
options: Increase the angle of attack and add power
Keep the angle of attack and add power
Decrease the angle of attack and add power
Increase the angle of attack and keep the power unchanged

questions.text: Where does interference drag typically arise?
options: Where two parts of the airframe meet, for example at the wing root where the wing joins the fuselage
Along the smooth, undisturbed middle of the upper wing surface
At the wing tips, as a result of tip vortices
Inside the boundary layer, as a result of skin friction

questions.text: As air flows back along an aerofoil, at which point does the boundary layer change from laminar to turbulent?
options: The transition point
The stagnation point
The separation point
The point of maximum thickness
